note: Configure an external identity provider (OIDC) so users can sign in with your organization's SSO. Local accounts keep working alongside it.
unavailable: Authentication settings require an administrator account.
empty: No identity provider configured. Add one to enable SSO sign-in.

idpHint.entra: Register Yagra as an application in Entra ID and paste its directory (tenant) ID below. Only the standard OIDC scopes are requested — Entra refuses any other, and the sign-in page never appears. To map roles from groups, turn on the groups claim under the app registration's Token configuration; the claim arrives as group object IDs.
idpHint.okta: Register Yagra as an OIDC web application in Okta. Yagra signs in against your org authorization server, which serves group membership directly. A custom authorization server has its own issuer URL and needs a groups claim configured on it — use "Other" for that.
idpHint.google: Create an OAuth client for a web application in Google Cloud. Google Workspace does not put group membership in the ID token, so roles cannot be mapped from groups — set a default role below to decide what everyone signing in becomes.
idpHint.generic: Enter the provider's details by hand. Use this for any IdP not listed above, and for an Okta custom authorization server.

delete.title: Delete provider
delete.confirm: Delete the SSO provider "{{name}}"? Users who sign in via SSO will no longer be able to.

field.name: Display name
field.issuerHint: The provider's base URL; discovery reads {issuer}/.well-known/openid-configuration.
field.issuerUnrecognized: This provider's issuer is not one this form builds — it is shown as stored and is left alone unless you change it. Pick the provider again above to switch to its own field.
field.tenantHint: From the app registration's Overview. A verified domain (contoso.onmicrosoft.com) works too.
field.domainHint: Your Okta org, without https:// and without a path.
field.clientSecretHint: Encrypted at rest and never shown again.
field.redirectUriHint: Register this exact URL at the IdP as an allowed redirect.
field.groupsClaimHint: The ID-token claim that carries the user's groups (default: groups).
field.roleMapHint: Map IdP group names to Yagra roles. The highest matching role wins.
field.noGroups: This provider does not put group membership in the ID token, so there is nothing to map. Every account that signs in gets the default role below.
field.defaultRoleNone: None — deny if no group maps
field.defaultRoleHint: Role for a user whose groups don't match any mapping.
field.defaultRoleRequired: Required for this provider: it is the role every account that signs in will get. Leaving it unset would deny everyone.

ldap.title: Directory (LDAP/AD)
ldap.note: Sign in with a corporate LDAP or Active Directory account. Yagra searches for the person with a service account, then re-binds as the entry it found — it never builds a DN from the typed name. Local accounts are always tried first, so a directory that is unreachable can never lock out an administrator.

field.replacePasswordHint: A password is stored. Tick to enter a new one; leave it alone to keep the stored one.
field.groupSearchHint: Leave the group fields empty to read membership from the user entry alone. Fill both to also search for groups — on Active Directory that is the only way to see nested groups, using (member:1.2.840.113556.1.4.1941:={user_dn}).
field.roleMapHint: Match a group by its full DN or just its name; case is ignored. The highest matching role wins.
field.enabledHint: While this is off, directory accounts cannot sign in and their existing sessions are revoked.

test.saveFirst: Save the directory before testing it — the check exercises what is stored.
test.role: This account would sign in as {{role}}.
test.denied: This account would be DENIED — no group maps to a role and there is no default role.

err.port: The port must be a number between 1 and 65535.
err.bindDn: The service account's DN is required.
err.bindPassword: A service account password is required. It cannot be blank — an empty password would make the search anonymous.
err.userBaseDn: A user base DN is required.
err.userFilter: The user filter must contain {username}, or it matches every entry under the base DN.
err.groupPair: A group search needs both a group base DN and a group filter, or neither.
err.groupFilter: The group filter must contain {user_dn} (or {username}) so it matches one person.
err.noMapping: Enabling the directory needs at least one group mapping or a default role — otherwise every login is denied.
err.save: Could not save the directory settings.

redirectUriMismatch: ⚠️ A configured SSO redirect URI does not match the address you are using. Yagra now serves the WebUI over HTTPS, so the stored redirect URI and the one registered at your identity provider both need updating — sign-in will fail at the callback until they do. Yagra will not change it for you: where an identity provider may send an authorization code is not something an upgrade should decide.
